d:
Some cities are born great. Others become great because they refused to stay invisible.
Navi Mumbai was always the quiet neighbour. The one people drove past on their way to 'real' Mumbai. A place you passed through, never arrived at.
Then something shifted. A bridge turned hours into minutes. An airport turned distance into access.
And suddenly, a city that was once defined by what it wasn't—not Mumbai, not central, not important—finally started defining itself.
New roads. New businesses. New energy.
The skyline changed. The economy changed. The identity changed.
